name: Sarnova / Digitech
desc:
Patient Research Specialist | Est. $19/hr | Research and Data Verification Heavy, No Sales Expectations
Company: Digitech (part of the Sarnova family of companies)
Industry: Health Science

What Your Day Will Look Like:
Digitech handles billing for ambulance (EMS) companies. Before an ambulance claim can be billed, someone has to make sure the patient and insurance information is right, and that's this job. You'll open patient care reports from ambulance crews, check the patient's name, date of birth, and address, and confirm their insurance was active on the day of the ride. When something is missing or doesn't match, you'll search internal systems, online tools, and insurance company resources to find the right answer and fix it before the claim moves on to coding. You'll document everything you find, work with the Coding, QA, and Client Services teams when questions come up, and keep up with daily and weekly volume goals. Expect to work across two monitors and several programs at once.

Soft Skills
- Attention to detail
- Persistence when information is hard to find
- Time management under deadlines
- Clear, organized written notes
- Comfort asking questions
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma or equivalent
Required Experience: None listed
Preferred Experience: None listed. Medical billing, insurance verification, or data entry background would help a resume stand out.

Required Skills:
- Multitasking with accuracy
- Able to work independently and stay focused in a remote, deadline-driven job
- Professional communication with other departments and outside partners
- Strong computer skills, comfortable with dual monitors and several systems at once
- Strong attention to detail and follow-through
- Clear written communication and grammar
- Reliable, punctual, and accountable
- Quick learner who takes organized notes during training

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Likes researching and tracking down missing information
- Has done data entry, insurance verification, or medical office work
- Works well alone and likes hitting clear daily goals
- Wants to get started in medical billing without a certification

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Gets frustrated by repetitive, detail-heavy work
- Isn't comfortable juggling several computer programs at once
- Wants lots of people contact during the day
- Struggles to meet production goals or tight deadlines
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening went, expect an email to schedule an interview
This is an estimated process.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Insurance verification
- Eligibility verification
- Patient demographics
- Data entry accuracy
- Medical billing
- Claims preparation
- Payer research
- Revenue cycle
- HIPAA
- Productivity and turnaround goals

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about your experience with data entry, insurance verification, or medical billing.
- How do you keep your work accurate when you're moving fast to hit a goal?
- What would you do if you couldn't find a patient's insurance information?
- Tell us about a time you caught a mistake in data before it caused a problem. What was the situation, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you had to learn a new computer system quickly. What was the situation, how did you learn it, and how did it turn out?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: Est. $18 to $20/hr, working estimate $19/hr. Pay isn't listed in the posting. This estimate is based on salary site data for Digitech billing and verification roles (about $36K to $50K a year). Hourly position.
-Shift: Must have availability for any shift based on business needs. Can be discussed in final interview, offer stage.
-Benefits: Comprehensive benefits package with a 401(k) plan. Details not listed.
-Equipment Provided: Not stated. Ask about the computer and dual monitors in the interview.
-Felony Friendly?: Case by case
-Drug Test: Certain positions
-Notes: This is a solid entry point into medical billing. It only requires a high school diploma, lists no required experience, and is fully remote across the United States. Daily and weekly production goals are tracked, so participants should be ready to keep a steady pace. Training length and camera requirements are not listed.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Patient Research Specialist → Insurance Account Resolution Specialist → Claims Resolution or Billing Specialist → Billing Team Lead → Revenue Cycle Supervisor. This role builds insurance verification, data accuracy, and billing workflow skills.
